why: The A 11 is right: Wahapedia's Slaughterbound has Lacerator and daemonic claw A 6. Relentless Rage (Berzerker Warband) gives +1 (A 7 in every list), Berzerker Glaive another +1 (A 8 here, marked), and Possessed Lord adds +3, so 11. [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] until the end of the phase, once per battle, at the start of the Fight phase: all correct. Making it the list's own reading is right. But listWhy says 'the datasheet’s A 7 makes 10'. The datasheet's A is 6 (DATASHEETS leaves A out because it varies by list), and 7 already includes the detachment's +1. The fix below corrects only the listWhy wording. Two related notes. (1) The datasheet reading set:{A:'10'} has Relentless Rage baked in, so a future Slaughterbound list in another detachment would get a wrong A 10. set:{A:'+3'} (as Battle Protocols writes set:{A:'+2'}) would be right for every list and would make this listWhy unnecessary. That is the owner's call, since it changes the display. (2) readOf fingerprints only Possessed Lord's text. Changing Berzerker Glaive's or Relentless Rage's text does not make A 11 or A 10 stale (tested on a scratch copy).

fix.listWhy: its enhancement Berzerker Glaive: the Slaughterbound’s Lacerator and daemonic claw has A 8 in this list (its datasheet’s A 6, +1 from Relentless Rage, +1 from Berzerker Glaive, both marked), so Possessed Lord’s +3 makes 11 (without the Glaive, A 7 makes 10)

why: Matches the text (data.js = Wahapedia Magnus the Red): at the start of your opponent's Shooting phase, one enemy unit within 24" of this PSYKER; until the end of the phase its ranged weapons have [HAZARDOUS]. The effect is on the enemy unit's weapons, whatever they shoot at. So a 'When targeted' line on every unit of the list (no needs) is the right place, and that includes Magnus himself (selfWhen; he can be shot by that unit too). It adds nothing the text does not say. Ranged only, opponent's Shooting phase, until the end of the phase: correct. There is no psychic roll in this text, so none is needed. Rendered in pubstomper (8 units) and mucho-mutantes (9 lines), with the 'When targeted' counts +1. Those are the only changes against main's own render.

Errant’s Duty: ranged weapons of the model have [ASSAULT] (kind ranged, note [ASSAULT]). The re-roll of Advance rolls is not an attack effect, so leaving it out says nothing extra. The Bondsman army rule supplies the rest: the pick in your Command phase ('your Command phase' in when), one friendly ARMIGER model (needs Armiger, oneModel), until the start of your next Command phase (lasts:'round', which the app's dmLasts defines as exactly that). 'Faction: Imperial Knights' in needs is not in the words ('friendly ARMIGER model'), but only IMPERIAL KNIGHTS models have ARMIGER, so it narrows nothing. Optional, not required: 'within 12"' could go in when, as Master of Mechanisms and Omnissiah’s Blessing say their 3"; Clever Know-wotz, the precedent, leaves it out. Matches data.js and Wahapedia (verify/.cache/waha/ds) word for word. No list has an ARMIGER model today, so nothing shows (no snapshot changes, as expected). Note: readOf covers only the Duty text; changing the Bondsman army rule (e.g. its duration) does not make this reading stale (tested on a scratch copy).

where: ooga-booga · Big Mek in Mega Armour
why: More Dakka (Wahapedia Big Mek in Mega Armour): 'This unit’s ranged attacks have [Ignores Cover]'. Once the Big Mek leads Meganobz, that is the whole attached unit. In ooga-booga the Meganobz carry Kombi-weapons (Shoota, Kill Shot, Point Blank), and BSData/New Recruit mark IGNORES COVER only on the Big Mek's Kustom Mega-blasta and Tellyport Blasta. So the 'Every ranged attack' footnote is needed there. In the other list (shooty) the Meganobz have only Twin Killsaws, so they have no ranged weapons and need no footnote. The difference is caused by the list; the listWhy is accurate. The riled-up [SUSTAINED HITS 1] reading is now derived on the datasheet and still named in ooga-booga's list ('More Dakka'). The resolved output is unchanged from main.

Soul Sight (data.js = Wahapedia Librarian in Phobos Armour): 'Select one visible enemy unit. Ranged attacks that target that enemy unit have [IGNORES COVER].' That covers every ranged attack against that unit, whoever makes it. So an aura with no needs and no notSelf is right: the app gives it to every unit of the list, the Librarian's own included. The nerf-when render confirms this: every unit's ranged footnotes get it, plus the Damage-tab option. Those are the only changes against main's own render. 'Your Shooting phase … (its psychic roll)': right. It adds nothing; it leaves out only 'if this unit is not battle-shocked', which could optionally be added to when.

Checked line by line against main's. Readings are composed in the documented order: army rules on the unit's Rules line (case- and apostrophe-insensitive), each datasheet part, the first matching enhancement or upgrade across the list's detachments, the detachment rule and moreRules whose needs (all/any/none/rule) the resolved unit meets, then the entry's own. An entry list with names replaces the whole list in its order; null gives none. readOf, readBy and listWhy are stripped from every reading; READ keys are kept off the datasheet copy and the entry rest. Every one of the 155 datasheet readings reaches at least one unit (trace). The resolved lists equal main's except the 7 new readings. Every other table is equal once reading keys are stripped. Minor, non-blocking: (a) enhancements are matched by strict ===, not nm(), so an apostrophe variant would silently drop an enhancement's readings (none today); (b) a misspelt name in an entry's list resolves to nothing in resolveArmies, but verify/tables.js throws on it (tested); (c) helpers.js CODE_RULES.resolveArmies says 'fingerprints (readOf too) and readBy hidden' and does not name listWhy, which is also hidden.
